prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The monocular depth map shows a sloped ground plane along an outdoor agricultural dirt path and irrigated field, with a continuous bright-to-dark gradient indicating distance increasing from the foreground near the camera wearer's feet up toward the upper-left horizon. In frame 1, the camera wearer's raised hand holding a small clear plastic object is bright white within arm's reach (~0.3–0.5 m below and in front), a yellow agricultural sprayer tank sits on the ground to the right of the path at ~1.5–2 m, and another person in black stands ahead on the path to the upper left at ~6–8 m (~5–6 m beyond the sprayer). Across frames 1 to 5, as the camera wearer walks forward and turns their viewpoint slightly right and then left, the sprayer moves closer to ~1 m at the lower-right edge in frame 2 before leaving the view, while the other person approaches from ~6–8 m in frame 1 (mostly out of view in frame 2 except a foot at the top edge, ~3–4 m in frame 3, and out of view in frame 4 as the camera looks right across the furrowed field) to within arm's reach (~1–1.5 m) on the left in frame 5, walking past the camera wearer with their head and upper torso cropped out by the frame edges. The depth map clearly separates the foreground silhouettes of the wearer's hand, the upright sprayer, and the approaching person from the textured mud, puddles, and irrigation tubes that visually blend together in the RGB image. However, the depth map is unreliable for determining which way the other person faces or looks, flattens the fine 3D relief of soil furrows and drip lines into a smooth gradient, and blurs the boundary where the sprayer and the person's feet meet the ground.
descriptions.segmentation: The instance segmentation map isolates discrete foreground entities against an unlabelled black background representing the dirt path and irrigated crop field, identifying the camera wearer's own hand at the bottom of frames 1–5 (~0.3–0.5 m, within arm's reach) and the other person walking along the path on the left in frames 1, 3, and 5 as 'person', plus the ground-placed sprayer tank in frame 1 (~1.5–2 m ahead on the right) as 'fire hydrant'. Using RGB context, the other person is facing toward the camera wearer while walking down the path from ~6–8 m away in frame 1 (~5–6 m behind the sprayer) to ~3–4 m in frame 3 and ~1–1.5 m (within arm's reach to the left) in frame 5, though their head is consistently occluded by the top/left frame boundary so their gaze direction cannot be confirmed. As the camera wearer advances and pans right in frame 4 before panning back in frame 5, the sprayer disappears off the lower-right edge after frame 2 and the other person leaves the frame in frames 2 and 4 while the wearer's hand rises higher into the lower-right foreground in frame 4. Compared to the RGB strip, the segmentation map sharply delineates the exact 2D pixel footprints of the wearer's hand and the approaching person against the dark soil and shadows. However, it is unreliable in class labelling and completeness: it misclassifies the yellow sprayer as a 'fire hydrant' in frame 1, completely misses the partially occluded sprayer at the right edge of frame 2 and the person's foot at the top of frame 2, merges the small held plastic item into the wearer's 'person' hand mask, and fails to distinguish the wearer's own limbs from the other person's body.
descriptions.pose: The body and hand skeleton map is almost entirely black across all five frames, detecting only a single partial yellow body skeleton in frame 3 for the person in black located ~3–4 m ahead and to the upper left on the dirt path (~3 m beyond the camera wearer's hand at the bottom edge). In that third frame, the aligned limb keypoints trace the person's right side/leg extending downward along the path as they walk toward the camera wearer, while their head and upper shoulder joints are cut off at the top frame edge, leaving their head orientation and gaze unrecorded. Across the sequence, the map provides no spatial tracking of the camera wearer's own hands holding the small object within arm's reach (~0.3–0.5 m below at the bottom edge of frames 1–5), the ground sprayer (~1.5–2 m on the right in frame 1 and ~1 m at the right edge in frame 2), or the other person when they are farther away (~6–8 m in frame 1) or passing within ~1–1.5 m on the left in frame 5. While the single skeleton in frame 3 makes the linear articulation of the approaching person's dark-clothed torso and leg easier to see than in the dark RGB silhouette, the pose map is highly unreliable overall because severe self-occlusion, steep downward egocentric viewing angles, and frame-edge cropping cause complete detection failures for all hands and bodies in frames 1, 2, 4, and 5.
